title: Adversarial Attacks Expose Path-Dependent Failures in Discrete Medical Image Tokenizers
abstract: arXiv:2611.28078v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Discrete image tokenizers convert medical images into token sequences that downstream models either decode into an image for a classifier (the reconstruction path), classify directly (the token path), or feed to a generative multimodal model. We ask whether imperceptible input perturbations can break these systems through the tokenizer alone. We evaluate four tokenizers on three imaging modalities and extend the strongest attack to a deployed generative model. Our central finding is path-dependence: the same tokenizer fails in opposite ways depending on how its output is used. A supervised attack collapses diagnostic accuracy on the reconstruction path, with ROC AUC falling to $\leq 0.013$ at $\epsilon=2/255$ on all four tokenizers, while sparing the token path. An unsupervised, label-free attack does the reverse; its damage concentrates in the multi-codebook tokenizers, worst in MedITok, whose token-path AUC falls from 0.919 to 0.239.

translated_title: 对抗攻击揭示离散医学图像分词器中的路径依赖性失效
translated_abstract: 离散图像分词器将医学图像转换为token序列，下游模型可以将这些序列解码为图像供分类器使用（重建路径）、直接进行分类（token路径），或输入到生成式多模态模型中。我们探究仅通过分词器本身，不可察觉的输入扰动能否破坏这些系统。我们在三种成像模态上评估了四个分词器，并将最强的攻击扩展到一个已部署的生成模型上。我们的核心发现是路径依赖性：同一分词器会根据其输出的使用方式不同而以相反的方式失效。监督式攻击会使重建路径上的诊断准确率崩溃——在ε=2/255时，所有四个分词器的ROC AUC降至≤0.013——而token路径则不受影响。无监督的、无标签攻击则正好相反；其破坏集中在多码本分词器上，其中MedITok最严重，其token路径的AUC从0.919降至0.239。
tldr: 该研究揭示了对抗攻击对离散医学图像分词器的破坏具有路径依赖性：同一分词器在不同下游用途下以相反方式失效——监督攻击使重建路径的诊断AUC降至0.013以下却不影响token路径，而无监督无标签攻击则主要摧毁token路径（MedITok的AUC从0.919降至0.239）。
en_tdlr: This study reveals path-dependent failures in discrete medical image tokenizers under adversarial attacks: the same tokenizer fails in opposite ways depending on downstream usage—supervised attacks collapse the reconstruction path (AUC ≤ 0.013) while sparing the token path, whereas unsupervised label-free attacks primarily destroy the token path (MedITok's AUC drops from 0.919 to 0.239).
